recommendations.headline: Only 19% of calls end in an order while 55% stall as unresolved callbacks, and satisfaction is the biggest lever we have — satisfied calls win 72% of the time versus 10% for neutral and 2% for dissatisfied calls, far more than price moves the needle (69% of calls never even reach a price discussion).
behaviour: Price-shopping and quote comparison dominate calls (price_shopper 389, comparing_quotes 221) yet price is formally discussed in only 31% of calls (626/2037), with price_high still raised in 342 calls.
Stock availability is simultaneously the top customer need (395 mentions) and the most common objection (350 cases, only 15% win rate), showing visibility gaps are costing deals.

Dealers are 52% of volume (1052 calls) and convert reasonably (33% win); fabricators are fewer (261) but convert best (35%); 'unknown' segment is 26% of calls but wins only 14%, suggesting poor qualification.

Urgent and bulk buyers are sizable (urgent_buyer 211, bulk_buyer 212) and repeat buyers are common (183) but almost none are tagged loyal_to_us (10), meaning repeat business isn't being reinforced as loyalty.
Competitor mentions are frequent (JSW 24, NMDC 13, SAIL 13, Jindal 12) and when 'competitor_cheaper' is the objection, win rate drops to just 8%, the lowest of all objections.
satisfaction: Only 29% of calls are rated satisfied, 56% neutral and 10% dissatisfied, and win rate collapses sharply across these buckets (72% → 10% → 2%), so improving call experience likely matters more than discounting.

Rep execution gaps are large: 365 calls had no fixed follow-up set and 363 had slow or unclear answers — together these likely explain why 55% of calls (1118) end as vague callbacks instead of orders.

Price is rarely resolved on the call: 69% of calls (1411) don't discuss price at all, and even when they do, only 8% result in outright acceptance versus 19% still negotiating — slow or unclear pricing response is a satisfaction issue, not just a cost issue.
No-quote-sent (219 calls) and not-asking-for-the-order (137 calls) are frequent missed moments directly suppressing conversion, independent of price.

conversion.title: Close every call with a fixed next step
conversion.evidence: 365 calls had no follow-up fixed and 1118 calls (55%) end as 'callback' with no firm commitment
conversion.action: Mandate reps log a specific date/time for next contact or delivery on every call; managers audit CRM entries daily

conversion.title: Resolve stock questions on the call, not after
conversion.evidence: Stock availability is the #1 need (395) and #1 objection (350) with only 15% win rate when it stalls
conversion.action: Give reps real-time access to the stock/inventory system so they confirm availability and quantity instantly instead of 'will check and call back'

conversion.title: Send quotes immediately, every time
conversion.evidence: 219 calls had no quote sent at all; satisfied calls (72% win) often involved fast WhatsApp quotes
conversion.action: Make same-call or same-day WhatsApp quote mandatory; use system-generated rate cards to speed this up

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order
conversion.evidence: 137 calls show reps never asked for the order despite customer interest
conversion.action: Train reps to always end product/price discussions with a direct close question (e.g., 'Shall I book this for you?')

conversion.title: Build a stronger response to competitor comparisons
conversion.evidence: Competitor_cheaper objection has the lowest win rate of any objection (8%, 73 calls); JSW, SAIL, NMDC, Jindal are named competitors
conversion.action: Equip reps with a value script (quality, certification, stock reliability) rather than discounting; escalate price-match requests to manager approval only

conversion.title: Standardize what 'satisfied' calls do well
conversion.evidence: Satisfied calls convert at 72% vs 10% for neutral calls
conversion.action: Review recordings of satisfied calls (fast stock check, quick WhatsApp bill, clear rate) and turn them into a standard call script/checklist

conversion.title: Qualify 'unknown' segment callers faster
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment is 26% of calls (529) but converts at only 14%, well below dealer (33%) and fabricator (35%)
conversion.action: Train reps to ask 2-3 quick qualifying questions (segment, quantity, urgency) in the first minute to route the call correctly

offers.title: On-demand cutting/processing service
offers.why: Cutting_processing is the 4th highest need (215 mentions); multiple calls show custom-cut-size requests

offers.title: Same-day/urgent dispatch slot
offers.why: Urgent_buyer (211) and fast_delivery need (370) are both high-frequency; many 'well' calls involve immediate pickup/dispatch

offers.title: Consider a structured credit/BG-rotation facility
offers.why: Credit_terms objection (79 calls, 14% win) and needs_credit behaviour (95) persist; one call shows a 1300-ton/month customer asking for credit with no offer given

offers.title: Proactive WhatsApp rate & stock update service
offers.why: Regular_updates is a top need (255) and many calls stall waiting for a promised rate/update

offers.title: Automatic test-certificate/quality pack with every order
offers.why: Test_certificate need (144) and quality_doubt objection (141, 21% win) recur frequently, including TC/tag legibility complaints

offers.title: Flexible small/part-load orders
offers.why: Min_quantity objection (49) and small_quantity need (31) show unmet demand for flexible lot sizes

loyalty.title: Priority stock reservation for repeat buyers
loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyer accounts in CRM and hold agreed stock for them ahead of walk-in demand
loyalty.why: Repeat_buyer behaviour is notable (183 calls) but loyal_to_us is tagged in only 10 calls, showing repeat purchase isn't being converted into recognized loyalty

loyalty.title: Dedicated contact/account manager for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a named rep as single point of contact for high-volume dealer accounts
loyalty.why: Dealers are 52% of call volume (1052) and already convert well (33%); a dedicated contact can push this higher

loyalty.title: Faster quote SLA for referral and loyal customers
loyalty.how: Commit to quote turnaround within a set short window for tagged repeat/referral accounts
loyalty.why: Referral behaviour (14) is underused and no_quote_sent affects 219 calls overall

loyalty.title: Recognize long-term dealers with first-in-line loading
loyalty.how: Give priority loading/dispatch slots to accounts with proven order history
loyalty.why: Summary notes a long-term dealer following up on PO planning and dispatch reassurance, showing dependency on reliability, not price

loyalty.title: Consider milestone-based rotation credit for very large regular accounts
loyalty.how: Offer BG-based credit rotation (not price discount) tied to consistent monthly volume
loyalty.why: Example in data: a 1300-ton/80-ton-monthly railway-linked customer requested credit with no formal offer made

loyalty.title: Post-delivery check-in call
loyalty.how: Schedule a short follow-up call after each major delivery to confirm satisfaction and resolve issues early
loyalty.why: After_sales_support need is low-volume but present (31) and several complaint calls cite unresolved delivery/invoice issues

non_price_benefits.title: Wide stock across brands and sizes
non_price_benefits.why: Stock_availability is the top customer need (395) and customers frequently ask about specific brands (SAIL, Vizag, Tata, Apollo, Mahaveer)

non_price_benefits.title: Fast dispatch and flexible vehicle arrangement
non_price_benefits.why: Fast_delivery is the 2nd highest need (370); many successful calls feature same-day open-body vehicle dispatch

non_price_benefits.title: In-house cutting and custom sizing
non_price_benefits.why: Cutting_processing need (215) and multiple calls describe custom cut-size and part-load requests

non_price_benefits.title: Verified quality with test certificates
non_price_benefits.why: Test_certificate need (144) and quality_doubt objection (141) are frequent; several calls raise TC/tag/heat-number concerns

non_price_benefits.title: Proactive status and rate updates
non_price_benefits.why: Regular_updates need (255) and delivery_status intent (220 calls) show customers value being kept informed without chasing

non_price_benefits.title: Technical guidance on grade/size selection
non_price_benefits.why: Needs_technical_help (266) and technical_advice need (153) indicate many customers want expert input, not just a price

top_questions.question: Do you offer credit terms for large/monthly orders?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain standard payment terms clearly and offer to escalate qualifying high-volume accounts to management for a structured credit/rotation arrangement review

top_questions.question: Can you match a competitor's or referral's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Avoid committing to match on the call; highlight certified quality, stock reliability and service, and offer to check with a manager before responding

top_questions.question: Is this size/material in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check the live inventory system during the call and give a definite yes/no with quantity instead of promising to call back later

top_questions.question: Can you send the rate/quote on WhatsApp quickly?
top_questions.answer_tip: Generate and send the quote during or immediately after the call; confirm the customer has received it before ending contact

top_questions.question: Can you send the test certificate/MTC, and why does the tag look different?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm TC is issued with every dispatch, proactively share a sample/reference if asked, and address tag or batch-number concerns transparently

top_questions.question: Will prices come down soon, should I wait?
top_questions.answer_tip: Share only factual, general market trend information without promising a drop; redirect to current availability and value

top_questions.question: What is the delivery timeline and can you deliver to my site?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific committed date/time and confirm transport arrangements before the call ends, rather than 'will check and revert'

top_questions.question: Why was my rate different from an earlier quote or someone else's?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain quote validity periods and market fluctuations honestly, then promptly verify and send a single confirmed updated quote
